title: Add release notes style guide + examples (breaking vs non-breaking model changes)
author: Wei Chen
description: This PR publishes the customer-facing Release Notes taxonomy/style guide for model/version changes and adds concrete examples to reduce ambiguity around breaking vs non-breaking changes. This is intended to be the canonical reference for (a) Redwood Docs writers editing generated notes, (b) engineers authoring metadata change summaries, and (c) PM/Support reviewing public wording. The guide is aligned with the changelog generator categories and explicitly calls out redaction rules (public vs internal) so we don’t repeat the incident where incomplete/internal notes were briefly published. Scope: docs-only content and IA updates; no generator code changes in this PR. Includes: category definitions (Security / Breaking / Deprecation / Quality / Performance / Bugfix), severity language guidance, “what changed/why/risk/rollback” structure, and a breaking-change decision tree focused on API/contract compatibility (tokenizer, structured output schema, tool calling behavior, safety filters, prompt-format expectations). Also includes a set of example release notes for common events: version promotion, tokenizer bump, quantization profile change, runtime requirement change, rollout rollback, and deprecation announcement. Follow-ups: (1) link this guide directly from the release note preview artifact output (redwood PR-18452), (2) add a short checklist to the reviewer template in redwood-model-registry. Screenshots: not applicable (content-only).

review_conversation: Elliot Price (review): Can we be explicit that “Performance” claims must be phrased as relative/typical and not guarantee numbers unless backed by published benchmark methodology? Also please add an example of acceptable wording vs unacceptable marketing language.

Wei Chen (author): Added a subsection under Performance: “allowed phrasing” + “not allowed”. Also added an example note that says “typical latency improved in our internal eval harness” and explicitly calls out that results vary by prompt/sequence length.

Marissa Cole (review): Breaking-change definition needs to match what Console will surface. Specifically, if a model’s tool-calling schema tightens validation (e.g., enum restriction), that is breaking even if the endpoint is the same. Add that example + mention rollback guidance requirement.
Wei Chen (author): Added a breaking example under Structured Output / Tool Calling and updated the template section to require a “Rollback / mitigation” line for Breaking + Deprecation categories.

Connor O'Brien (review): Please add a checklist we can link in review flows: category chosen, severity chosen, “what changed/why/risk/rollback”, redaction verified. Also please mention that notes are generated from metadata/events and editors should avoid inventing details not present in the artifact.

Wei Chen (author): Added a short “Reviewer checklist” section and an “Editing generated notes” section that explicitly discourages adding details not present in the generator artifact; editors can clarify language but shouldn’t introduce new claims.

Naomi Feldman (security review): Good start. Add a clear list of prohibited content examples: internal incident IDs, specific customer names/accounts, internal-only metrics thresholds, vendor/hardware SKUs when it could reveal deployment topology. Also note that security-related changes must not imply exploitability details unless cleared.
Wei Chen (author): Added “Do not include” bullets + example redactions. Added note: Security category wording should be high-level unless Security approves expanded disclosure.

Kira Thompson (review): For Private customers, the ‘version’ they see may be an upgrade bundle. Can we add one example showing how we phrase notes that map to a bundle and mention that rollout timing differs by deployment mode?

Wei Chen (author): Added an example under Rollback/Upgrade: “Private bundle 2025.10.2 includes model X promotion…” and a line in the guide: “Availability and rollout timing may differ across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.”
Elliot Price (final): Approved. Please ensure PR-9312 references this guide from the landing page.
Wei Chen (author): Done in this PR by adding cross-links from release-notes/index.md.
